cut palmar branch of right median nerve in right wrist wound was found. The main trunk of the nerve was intact. The palmar branch of the median nerve was repaired and all wounds sutured ("1st Operation").

source: bone scan ... showed signs of reflex sympathetic dystrophy syndrome or now termed compression regional pain syndrome ("CRPS I").

manifestations.description: Decreased sensation over right palm and radial three digits
Total numbness in the whole of the palmar aspect and total numbness in the distal part of the right hand
Severe stiffness with loss of flexion in the fingers and thumb; greatly reduced grip
Significant muscle wasting of right arm and forearm and severe wasting of the muscles of the thenar eminence
Persistent pain and numbness over right hand
Diffuse tenderness and stiffness of neck
Straight leg raising test 30 degrees for the right side and 60 degrees for the left side

treatments_received: Emergency operation: repair of cut palmar branch of right median nerve (1st Operation)
Operation: release of carpal tunnel and relaxation of scar and web contracture of the skin (2nd Operation)
MRI scans, nerve conduction test attempted, bone scan

losses.description: Unable to return to his pre-Accident employment and "could only work solely as an interpreter."
Permanent impairment and reduced function of the dominant right hand including numbness, stiffness, reduced grip and muscle wasting.
